source.title: Scalable Autoregressive Image Generation with Mamba
source.authors: Haopeng Li; Jin-Yue Yang; Ke-Xin Wang; Xue-Rui Qiu; Yu-Hong Chou; Xin Li; Guo-Qi Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses language-model scaling laws as background but does not test held-out language-model loss or a power-law relationship. Its image-generation scaling results use FID, not loss, and do not fit or test a power law.
record.gate_note: The paper reports FID for AiM models at different parameter counts and describes FID trends with training steps and compute. These are related image-generation scaling findings, but FID results do not measure the loss or power-law form named by the claim versions. The language-model scaling results mentioned in the text are citations, not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. and Hoffmann et al. only in its introduction. Its own scaling results are image-generation FID across four AiM sizes (148M–1.3B) and over training steps and compute. It fits no power law, reports no held-out loss, and runs no extrapolation, allocation or shape test at fixed parameters. The FID trend is a related finding, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that AiM scales: larger models and longer training each improve FID. They also say larger models use compute more efficiently, and they did not go beyond 1.3B because of ImageNet1K constraints.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Mamba-based autoregressive image generators on ImageNet and evaluates image quality with FID; it does not use the language-model held-out-loss measurement or fit the power laws in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that FID changes with model size and training steps, but does not report sensitivity of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations to setup or fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: AiM image-generation FID falls from 3.52 (148M) to 2.21 (1.3B). The paper reports a correlation near -0.9838 between FID and parameter count, and says FID falls with more training steps for all sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For Mamba-based autoregressive class-conditional ImageNet generators, FID improves monotonically with model size and training. This is not a fitted power law in loss.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is for image-generation FID rather than held-out loss. The paper does not fit a power law or report exponents, and the scaling plots provide no exact point values in the text. The authors state that ImageNet1K constraints prevented scaling model size to 2B or larger.

untested.parts: Held-out language-model loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of small-run fits to larger runs.
Shape effects at a fixed parameter count. Depth and width vary together with size here, and the adaLN ablations change the parameter count.
A power-law form in loss for image models. Only FID is reported and no fit is made.
Downstream task performance of language models versus scale or loss.
Sensitivity of exponents or splits to setup and fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only', because scaling-law papers appear only as a single introductory citation. The training loss is next-token negative log-likelihood, but no loss values are reported. The 2B+ limit is the authors' choice, not a scaling failure.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power laws fitted on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations and their trends with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices on held-out language-model loss at fixed parameter count.
Whether held-out loss follows the same power-law form in other modalities or training regimes; this paper reports image-generation FID, not held-out loss or a fitted power law.
Downstream task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

rows.note: The reported correlation concerns FID and parameter count; it is not a fitted power law in loss.
rows.check: This is a correlation between FID and parameter count over only four models. The Figure 6 axis appears logarithmic, but no power-law form or exponent is fitted. It cannot show the power-law form in V1 or V5.

rows.note: The text states that FID decreases with additional training steps across all models; individual curve values are not stated.
rows.check: The state 'observed' refers to FID falling, which no version names. Against the claim's versions the state cannot be determined, because the measure is FID, not loss, and the result is figure-only.
